market_context: United States; refrigerator storage of commercial and homemade kefir.
title: How Long Does Kefir Last in the Fridge?

seo.title: How Long Does Kefir Last in the Fridge?
seo.meta_description: Follow the package date for commercial kefir, keep it at 40°F/4°C or below, and discard it for mold, abnormal spoilage odors, or suspicious growth.
seo.search_intent: Know how to store kefir in the refrigerator and recognize spoilage.

excerpt: There is no single shelf-life number for every kefir. Commercial products should follow the package date and after-opening directions; homemade batches vary with culture and hygiene. Keep either type cold, covered, and discard it if mold or clearly abnormal spoilage appears.
content_html:
Kefir is acidic and fermented, but that does not make it immune to spoilage. Refrigeration slows microbial activity; it does not stop it completely. That is why the answer depends on whether you bought the kefir or fermented it yourself.

For commercial kefir, the label comes first

When the container is unopened and has stayed refrigerated, use the manufacturer’s date as the primary guide. After opening, follow any shorter use-within period printed on the package.

Store kefir at 40°F (4°C) or below in a consistently cold part of the refrigerator rather than the door, where temperatures swing more often.

Homemade kefir varies more

Culture strength, fermentation time, temperature, container cleanliness, and handling differ from kitchen to kitchen, so a universal number would give false precision.

Once the flavor is where you want it, removing the grains and chilling the kefir slows fermentation. It may still become more tart and separate over time.

Separation is not the same as mold

A yellowish whey layer with a thicker white portion can be a normal acid-driven separation and often mixes back together. Fuzzy growth, unusual colors, or a clearly rotten odor are different and should trigger disposal.

Do not rescue a moldy batch

If mold or suspicious surface growth is present, do not scoop off the top and keep the rest. A fermented dairy product with visible contamination is not worth testing by taste.

Time matters, but cold storage and clean handling matter just as much.

faq.question: Is it normal for kefir to separate in the fridge?
faq.answer: Yes. Whey separation can happen as acidity increases and does not by itself mean spoilage.

faq.question: Can I remove a little mold and use the rest?
faq.answer: No. Visible mold or unusual surface growth is a reason to discard the whole product.

faq.question: Where should kefir be stored?
faq.answer: In a cold, stable area of the refrigerator at 40°F/4°C or below, tightly covered.
